sourceName: National Health and Aging Trends Study
policyPurpose: Define the minimum disclosure-control gate for any NHATS-derived cohort-flow, endpoint-route, missingness, survey-design or aggregate functional-survival output before it can leave a governed workspace or enter the public Human Infra Web layer.

currentDecision.reason: The disclosure policy is registered, but no real NHATS data, exact variables, route counts, survey-design plan, governed workspace or disclosure report exists. Only synthetic validator tests are allowed.

rules.smallCellRule: For public export, every cell with count below 5 must be suppressed before output. Unsuppressed counts below 5 block export.
rules.rowLevelRule: Row-level records, participant identifiers, join keys, interview rows and record-level extracts cannot be exported from the governed workspace.
rules.publicAiUploadRule: NHATS/NSOC data and any output that could expose NHATS row-level or small-cell information cannot be uploaded to public LLM or AI platforms.

validatorContract.currentBoundary: synthetic validator only; no real NHATS rows, route counts or cell counts are present in repository

prohibitedActions: Do not export row-level NHATS records.
Do not upload NHATS data or unsafe derived outputs to public AI systems.
Do not publicly export unsuppressed cells with count below 5.
Do not use disclosure validation as evidence of model calibration, predictive validity, causal effect or individual usefulness.
Do not output individual death dates, personal medical advice or personal longevity rankings.
nextWork: Run the synthetic validator and publish only the generated validator report.
After governed access exists, bind real outputs to the same policy before any public export.
Keep disclosure-control validation separate from model calibration and survey-design validation.
